annotation_provenance.author: AI annotation reviewer
annotation_provenance.construction: Sixteen new anonymous source profiles and their judgments were authored before any outputs from the audit implementation were inspected. Existing diagnostic schema and annotation semantics were read for compatibility; no existing profile text or judgment was copied. Prior development failures motivated topic selection.
annotation_provenance.purpose: Paired checks of a shared evidence standard, requirement depth, counterclaims, omitted positive associations, exclusion of contextual units from duration and bounded usage arithmetic.
annotation_provenance.limits: One agent authored and reviewed the examples. These are targeted synthetic diagnostics, not independent human annotations, a representative recruitment benchmark or an untouched generalization test. Freeze the bytes before model evaluation; report disagreements without changing labels to fit outputs.

semantics.criterion_labels: Role: followed by role.replace('_', ' '); Required skill: followed by ' or '.join(group); Total employment; skill + ' duration'; Preferred skill: followed by skill. All skill identifiers retain the normalized lower-case spelling in requirements.

status.supported: The supplied resume supports the exact requested condition under the declared evidence basis; this is a claim in source, not external verification.
status.not_demonstrated: Complete supplied context fails to demonstrate the requested condition or explicitly excludes it; this is not a claim about all of the person's real abilities.
status.uncertain: Attribution, depth, duration placement, criterion interpretation, or conflicting source claims prevent a supported/negative decision.

semantics.multiple_allowed_statuses: Only used where either conservative insufficiency category is defensible. Supported is deliberately excluded for unsupported application claims.

relationship.direct: The candidate's evidence directly supports the named technology or exact role/capability.
relationship.equivalent: The candidate's own described work supports the requested capability or role through a stated semantic equivalence; no unsupported named-product substitution.
relationship.related: Relevant neighboring technology or work context that does not by itself satisfy the exact requested condition.
relationship.none: No usable personal relationship supports the condition. A global/team mention without personal attribution can have no qualifying relationship.
relationship.null: Relationship category is not material for this criterion, usually arithmetic.

durations.explicit_ended_months: An explicit ended range includes both named months: 2020-01 through 2023-12 is 48 months. Compute unions of calendar-month intervals; do not add overlapping employment twice.
durations.current_employment: Present/current ends at the frozen 2026-09-01 boundary. January 2024 through that boundary contributes 32 completed months; do not include the incomplete September month.
durations.null_bounds: No duration is requested or safely identifiable for that criterion. Null is not zero. Both bounds may be null when a one-off task cannot establish a usage duration.
durations.numeric_bounds: Exact claims use equal minimum and maximum. Different bounds represent defensible source-derived uncertainty about union placement; they are not model confidence intervals.
durations.total_employment: Union of dated employment in any occupation under these requests; education and personal projects do not add employment months.
durations.skill_related_employment: Employment intervals linked to a skill-specific title and sustained responsibilities under an explicitly related-employment request. This does not assert independently verified continuous usage.
durations.explicit_usage: An explicit bounded usage claim, named subinterval, or whole-role usage statement; apply limiting statements before arithmetic.
durations.explicit_usage_union_bounds: Union bounds for separate explicit usage claims whose placement inside overlapping roles is unknown.

semantics.source_fragments: Fragments are verbatim diagnostic anchors, not required contiguous generated citations. Separate fragments may need separate exact offsets. Their presence does not replace contextual entailment. Counterevidence must also be considered; absence findings require coverage of the complete supplied resume.
semantics.metamorphic_pairs: Invariant pairs change wording, layout, record order, or untrusted instructions while preserving declared criterion outcomes and numeric bounds. Selective-change and criteria-change pairs deliberately alter only the identified semantic condition.
semantics.review_independence: Every expected criterion applies to a fresh complete-source assessment, including negative and uncertain findings. A first-pass summary or fixed extraction omission cannot override supplied evidence.
semantics.positive_associations: Expected positive duration associations identify source facts that must survive assessment and audit. Match source meaning and dates, not invented unit IDs or model wording. Every listed association is required when must_find_all_positive_associations is true. A source claim remains unverified employment history.
semantics.excluded_duration_source_fragments: These exact fragments identify context that must not contribute duration credit or suppress an independent accepted association. They can be cited as contrary or contextual evidence.
semantics.association_evaluation_scope: The legacy evaluator reads the compatible status, relationship, basis and numeric fields. It does not automatically assert positive_associations or excluded_duration_source_fragments; a run that omits those checks must say so.
semantics.cross_candidate_pairs: Each group uses identical structured requirements and semantic_brief for both profiles. Invariant groups preserve expected status and duration; contrast groups change only the named evidence condition. Equivalence of support does not require identical wording or identical relationship labels unless explicitly specified.

pairs.judgment: Both profiles provide personal database implementation. The second must not be held to an unrequested handwritten-query standard.
The shared standard requests direct authorship; changing the source authorship claim must change the result.
Project-scoped technology evidence can support the requested application. A global skills list cannot inherit the same depth.
The first profile remains unresolved because its source contradicts itself. The second has corroborating personal attribution.
Both positive work associations must remain discoverable. Omitting either role changes the supported duration and can change the threshold verdict.
The same independent thirty-six-month employment association survives both kinds of additional context. Neither context adds duration credit.
Both sources establish personal Go work. The explicit quantity changes only the duration threshold outcome.
The two profiles differ in duration knowledge. A supported application can coexist with unknown duration or a documented duration below the requirement.
